results.reason: Issue 1 puts the Section 3.2 deadline at about Aug. 16, 2026 and treats it as passed, since Sched. 3.12 says only that the Company 'intends' to send notice. It says the agreement expires Nov. 14, 2026, before the Nov. 30 closing. It calls the MIPA §3.12(c) rep untrue and the schedule note thin cover, with indemnity and termination exposure for Sellers.

Issue 2 identifies the 100% equity sale as a Change of Control under DA §1.3(a) and §14.2 requiring prior written consent, with an immediate termination right under §14.3. It notes the consent is omitted from Sched. 3.6 and so falls outside §6.4 and §7.1(d). It recommends obtaining consent before Closing and adding it to Sched. 3.6.

Issue 5 notes SL §1.1 adds New York and Virginia and that DA §19.4 ranks the Side Letter above the DA body. It says the non-compete covers six states while exclusivity covers four. It recommends conforming the non-compete to four states or extending exclusivity. The post-term tail is addressed in Issue 3.

Issue 5 identifies the conflict between SL New York law and New York County courts and DA Delaware law and Wilmington courts. It explains that a single dispute could split between forums and recommends conforming to Delaware.
The response states the Initial Term ends November 14, 2026 (DA §3.1).
The response states the Target Closing is November 30, 2026.
The response refers only to a 'four-state Territory' and never names Delaware, Maryland, New Jersey and Pennsylvania.
The response is a memo to the Supervising Partner. Each issue has Where, Why it matters and Recommendation sections.
Issues are labeled 'Most Significant First' with severity tags. Section 4 expressly lists items to raise with the client and with Quillon's counsel.
The response says the DA 'does not renew automatically' and that a notice sent now would be late. It does not claim renewal or that a timely notice is still possible.
The response states the consent is not on Sched. 3.6 and not covered by §6.4 or §7.1(d).
